1.explanation: The core of the issue lives in the React Dropdown component’s render method: it unconditionally renders <ListBox.Field tabIndex="0" …>, overriding any incoming tabIndex and ignoring the disabled state. The ListBoxField component itself applies tabIndex based on rest.tabIndex || -1, so if Dropdown passed down -1 it would work. By hard-coding 0, the disabled dropdown still yields a focusable child. To fix this, Dropdown.render should compute and pass the correct tabIndex (e.g. -1 when disabled) or omit the hard-coded value so ListBoxField’s default logic can apply.
1.bug_scenario: When a <Dropdown> is rendered with disabled=true and tabIndex="-1", the outer dropdown does receive tabIndex=-1 but its inner ListBox.Field still has tabIndex=0. As a result, even though the control is disabled, its child remains focusable via the Tab key, breaking keyboard navigation flow.

2.explanation: The bug manifests because the React `Dropdown` render method always injects `tabIndex="0"` on the inner field regardless of the `disabled` or outer `tabIndex` props. The `ListBoxField` component is responsible for setting its own `tabIndex` (falling back to -1) based on incoming props, but it never receives an override from the parent because `Dropdown` hard-codes `tabIndex="0"`. To fix the problem, the render method in `packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js` must pass a conditional `tabIndex`: when `disabled` or `tabIndex={-1}` is specified at the top, it should override the inner field’s `tabIndex` instead of always setting it to `0`. In parallel, `ListBoxField` already supports a `rest.tabIndex` prop and will properly render `-1` when provided, so updating the parent render to forward the correct `tabIndex` will ensure disabled dropdowns become unfocusable as expected.
2.bug_scenario: In the React `<Dropdown>` component when `disabled = true` and `tabIndex = -1` are passed in, the outer `<div>` wrapper (the `ListBox` container) correctly renders with `tabIndex="-1"`, but its child field element still has `tabIndex="0"`. In the inspector screenshot you can see the root listbox is unfocusable, yet the nested `<div role='combobox'>` (the clickable field) remains in the tab order despite being disabled, breaking expected keyboard navigation.
